The '''38th [[Academy Awards]]''', honoring the [[1965 in film|best in film for 1965]], were held on April 18, 1966, at the [[Santa Monica Civic Auditorium]] in [[Santa Monica, California]].  They were hosted by [[Bob Hope]], and were the first Oscars to be broadcast live [[Color television|in color]].<ref name="Oscars '65 Notes"/> [[Lynda Bird Johnson Robb|Lynda Bird Johnson]], daughter of [[Lyndon B. Johnson|President Lyndon B. Johnson]], attended the ceremony, escorted by actor [[George Hamilton (actor)|George Hamilton]].<ref name="Oscars '65 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/844/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=844 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref>

The most successful films of the year were ''[[The Sound of Music (film)|The Sound of Music]]'' and ''[[Doctor Zhivago (film)|Doctor Zhivago]]'', each with ten nominations and five wins, with the former winning [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]]. Both films are in the top 10 inflation-adjusted  commercially successful films ever made,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/adjusted.htm |title=All Time Box Office Adjusted for Ticket Price Inflation |publisher=Boxofficemojo.com |access-date=2012-08-14 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504000735/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/adjusted.htm |archive-date=2009-05-04 }}</ref> and both would go on to appear on the [[American Film Institute]] list of the [[AFI's 100 Years...100 Movies|greatest American films of the twentieth century]].

''The Sound of Music'' was the first Best Picture winner without a screenwriting nomination since ''[[Hamlet (1948 film)|Hamlet]]'', and would be the last until ''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]'' at the [[70th Academy Awards]]. ''[[Othello (1965 British film)|Othello]]'' became the third film (of four to date) to receive four acting nominations without one for Best Picture. [[William Wyler]] received the last of his record twelve [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] nominations for ''[[The Collector (1965 film)|The Collector]]''.

== Multiple nominations and awards ==
{{Col-begin}}
{{Col-1-of-2}}
These films had multiple nominations:

*''10 nominations'': ''[[Doctor Zhivago (film)|Doctor Zhivago]]'' and ''[[The Sound of Music (film)|The Sound of Music]]''
*''8 nominations:'' ''[[Ship of Fools (film)|Ship of Fools]]''
*''5 nominations:'' ''[[The Agony and the Ecstasy (film)|The Agony and the Ecstasy]]'', ''[[Cat Ballou]]'', ''[[Darling (1965 film)|Darling]]'', ''[[The Great Race]]'', ''[[The Greatest Story Ever Told]]'' and ''[[A Patch of Blue]]''
*''4 nominations:'' ''[[Othello (1965 British film)|Othello]]'', ''[[A Thousand Clowns]]'' and ''[[The Umbrellas of Cherbourg]]''
*''3 nominations:'' ''[[The Collector (1965 film)|The Collector]]'' and ''[[Inside Daisy Clover]]''
*''2 nominations:'' ''[[The Flight of the Phoenix (1965 film)|The Flight of the Phoenix]]'', ''[[King Rat (film)|King Rat]]'', ''[[Morituri (1965 film)|Morituri]]'', ''[[The Slender Thread]]'' and ''[[The Spy Who Came In from the Cold (film)|The Spy Who Came In from the Cold]]''

{{Col-2-of-2}}
The following films received multiple awards.

*''5 wins'': ''[[Doctor Zhivago (film)|Doctor Zhivago]]'' and ''[[The Sound of Music (film)|The Sound of Music]]''
*''3 wins'': ''[[Darling (1965 film)|Darling]]''
*''2 wins:'' ''[[Ship of Fools (film)|Ship of Fools]]''

{{Col-end}}
